patch.description:
Takes ONE field, `name`. A token's scopes, capabilities, scope grants and constraints are fixed at the moment it is minted and cannot be changed afterwards — so a token you audited stays the token you audited, and a token whose reach is wrong is replaced rather than edited (`POST /pats` for a new one, `POST /pats/{id}/rotate` to change the secret while keeping the grants). Sending any other field is a 422 naming it.

**Requires token scope: `admin`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

get.description:
Everything we hold about the CALLER as one downloadable JSON document: profile, memberships, sessions, posts, topics, pages, custom-field values and consent records. Served as an attachment, synchronously — it is a database read, not a job, so there is nothing to poll. Scoped to the caller’s own account and no other; the organization-wide equivalent is `GET /orgs/{orgId}/export`, and the orchestrator-driven one is `/privacy/executor/{orgId}/*`.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

post.description:
IRREVERSIBLE. Anonymises the caller’s account and revokes every session, including the one making the request — the session cookie is cleared in the response, so a client must treat a 200 as a logout. Confirmation is the account’s own email address in `confirm` (credentials live in Atlas, so there is no local password to re-check and a live session is what proves the human); anything else is a 400. Content the account authored is detached from it rather than deleted, so a forum thread does not lose its replies. Export first with `GET /users/me/export` — afterwards there is nothing left to export.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Which page shape to apply. A shape adds named slots to what a piece of this space is made of; it is NOT the reader layout (that is `PUT …/preset`). `how-to` — One task, done. The goal, what you need first, the steps, and how to tell it worked. `tutorial` — Learning by building something end to end — for somebody who does not know the product yet. `reference` — What something is and exactly how it behaves — read in a hurry, by somebody who already knows why. `explanation` — Why something works the way it does — the page that stops the same question being asked forever. `troubleshooting` — One symptom, its cause, and the fix — written for somebody who is already annoyed. `bug-report` — What happened, what should have happened, and how to see it — the three things a fix needs. `feature-request` — The problem first, then the idea — so somebody can solve it a better way than you asked for. `question` — Asks for the context, what was already tried, and what was expected — the three things a good answer needs. `landing` — A wide opening statement, then the three things you want somebody to do next. `comparison` — Two things, side by side, and the honest sentence about when to pick each. `release` — What shipped, what it changes for a reader, and what to do if it broke something. `keepachangelog` — The standard changelog categories — Added, Changed, Fixed, and the rest — one list each. `incident` — What broke, who it hit, what you did, and what stops it happening again. `role` — The work, who it suits, what it pays, and how to apply. `policy` — A plain-English summary over the document itself, so somebody can read either. `announcement` — One thing, said properly: what it is, why now, and what a reader does about it. `faq-answer` — The answer first, then the reason, for the question you keep being asked.

onThisPage.description: Whether this document carries the "on this page" rail: `auto`, `always` or `never`. Beats the legal space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it. A page-backed document sets `onThisPage` on its page’s metadata instead.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Replaced whole on write; unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This document’s own `customCss`, partial `theme`, `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard` and `jsonLd`. Keys merge; `null` clears.

Every space with its collections, pages and topics, as one JSON attachment — the document `POST /orgs/{orgId}/import` takes, so an export of one organization is a migration into another. CONTENT, never credentials: no tokens, no secrets, no password hashes, no webhook signing keys, so an export is safe to hand to a customer and is not sufficient to clone an installation. post.description:
Takes the document `GET /orgs/{orgId}/export` produces and lands it here. Idempotent, matched by SLUG at every level — re-importing the same document updates what it already created rather than making a second copy of it — and additive: nothing in this organization is deleted because the document does not mention it. The reply is a per-level count of what was created and updated. For declaring the shape of a site rather than restoring content, see `PUT /orgs/{orgId}/manifest`, which dry-runs by default.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

patch.description:
The slug is the first segment of every public address this organization owns AND an accepted value for `{orgId}` on every route under `/orgs/{orgId}/…` — so a rename rewrites the public URLs and changes what the readable form of the path resolves to (the uuid never changes and keeps working). Globally unique; a reserved platform name is refused so a rename cannot shadow our own routes; capped at 63 characters because it is handed out as a DNS label. The reply carries `previous`, which is what a redirect or a cache purge needs.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Replaces this space’s theme wholesale — colours, type, element styles, the phone layer. Prefer the PATCH unless you are importing a complete theme, because a full write clears anything the stored theme had that your body omits.

A `motion.targets` entry naming an animation that is not a built-in, a keyframe in this theme, or a keyframe of the space’s site is refused: 422 `validation.failed` naming the key and listing every valid name. The answer carries `warnings` like the GET.

preset.description: The named layout the space's index wears. Valid values depend on the SPACE's type — see the table in this operation's description, or `GET /space-types/{type}/presets`. An unknown value is a 422 that lists the ones this type accepts.

piecePreset.description: The named layout ONE piece of the space wears. Only some types offer a choice; for the others any value is a 422 saying so. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` lists them per type.

frontDoor.description: The front door's knobs, by key. Only the keys this SPACE's type declares, of the kind it declares — a toggle takes a boolean, a choice takes one of its values — plus `sectionOrder`. An unknown key is a 422 that names it and lists the ones this type has. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` serves the whole set as data under `frontDoor`.

put.description:
**The layouts each type accepts.** `preset` and `piecePreset` are validated against the
space's own type, so the same word is legal for one space and a 422 for another. The same list is
served as data by `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` (and `GET /space-types/presets` for all of
them at once), which is the one to read if you are generating configuration. That route answers
FOUR vocabularies — `presets`, `piecePresets`, `shapePresets` and `frontDoor` (the keys the
type's front door accepts, and the values each one takes).

| Space type | Field | Value | What it looks like |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `guide` *(default)* | The page tree beside the writing, an on-this-page rail, and previous/next at the foot. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `reference` | The tree and the page, nothing else — for material read in a hurry by somebody who knows why. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `minimal` | Just the page — no tree, no rail. For docs that are really one document. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `landing` | A front door: your intro, a search box, and each section as a card. Pages inside keep the Guide layout. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `categories` *(default)* | Category cards on the way in, threads inside each. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `firehose` | One stream, newest first — no cards on the way in. For communities that live in the flow. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `dense` | The stat table a big community reads at a glance: title and tags on the left, replies, views and freshness in columns. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `feed` *(default)* | One column, newest first, with the standfirst under each headline. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `grid` | A card grid led by the cover images. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `magazine` | The newest post writ large, the rest as a grid beneath it. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-clean` *(default)* | Nothing beside the words; more to read waits at the end. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-toc` | An on-this-page rail to the right — for long, structured pieces. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-suggested` | Other posts down the left, magazine-style. |
| `ROADMAP` | `preset` | `board` *(default)* | Columns by status, cards within them. |
| `ROADMAP` | `preset` | `list` | One column, grouped by status — reads top to bottom, best for long boards. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `timeline` *(default)* | Every entry in one dated line, newest first. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `releases` | Entries grouped under the version that shipped them. |
| `STATUS` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Current state on top, incident history beneath. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | The documents, in the order you put them. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `no-front-door` | No index page — each document is its own address, linked from wherever you use it. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `sectioned` *(default)* | Every answer open, grouped by topic, each with an anchor to link to. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `accordion` | Questions closed until asked — for a long list scanned by eye. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `list` *(default)* | Every open role in one list, location and kind beside each. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `departments` | Roles grouped under the team they join. |
| `CONTACT` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Your words above the form, expectations beside it. |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Upcoming events on top, past events beneath. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Modules of lessons, taken in order, with a progress bar and mark-complete. |
| `CUSTOM` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | A custom space is arranged by its own shape, not by a preset. |

from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

redirects.description: The whole table, replacing what is stored — except the rules the platform wrote itself when a page or a collection was renamed, which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

ids.description: Collection ids in the order you want them. value.body:
# Getting started

Install the SDK, then create your first page.

block-content.summary: Author with a block document — `content` as BlockDoc JSON

content.text: Install the SDK, then create your first page.

post.description:
Creates a page directly inside one collection, which is the usual authoring door: it saves you creating a page and then moving it, and the slug is derived from the title unless you name one.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

**A taken slug is reported, not hidden.** By default (`onSlugTaken: "suffix"`) a page whose slug already exists is created at `slug-2`, and the response says so: `slugChanged: { asked, used }` plus a sentence in `warnings[]` and on the `X-Field-Warnings` header. Send `onSlugTaken: "fail"` to get a `409 page.slug_taken` instead — a pipeline that wants to know about a collision should ask for it. `PATCH …/pages/{pageId}` takes the same option with the SAME default, so one rule covers both doors. See [Slugs](https://forumulate.com/guides/api-conventions#slugs).

**Send ONE body field.** `content` (block JSON) is exclusive with `body` and `sections` (Markdown); sending `content` alongside either is a 422 naming both. It used to accept them together and silently discard the block document. `body` and `sections` together remain legal — that is the designed authoring path (slots first, then trailing prose).

**A `parentId` must exist here.** A page id that is not a live page in this space is a 404, and one in another collection is a 422. A nil uuid used to be stored, producing a row that never appeared in the tree.

**A `sections` key must be a slot this space type declares.** An unknown key is a 422 listing the slots that exist; it used to create one that nothing renders.

Read a page: its id, metadata, `status` (`published`/`draft`), and a stable `contentHash` of the published body — so a docs-as-code pipeline can detect drift (a UI edit since it last pushed) without downloading the document. Add `?include=content` to also get the live block document as `content`.

`status` is derived from the LIVE revision (`published` once anything has been published), so it does not change when a newer draft is saved — read `hasDraft` and `draftUpdatedAt` for that. Both were missing, and a pipeline reading `published` on a page whose latest work was unpublished had no way to tell.

onThisPage.description: Whether THIS page carries the "on this page" rail: `auto` (the surface default), `always` or `never`. Beats the space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` or absent means the space decides.

fields.description: The parameters this page’s space type declares. PATCH semantics: the keys you send are merged into the fields already stored, so sending one field leaves the rest alone, and `null` clears a field. The declared keys, their labels, kinds and options are at `GET /space-types/{TYPE}` under `fields` — for a DOCS page they are `audience` (labelled "Written for"), `appliesTo` and `deprecated`. An undeclared key is refused with a 422 naming the keys that do exist.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Replaced whole on write; unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

editorial.description: Your claim that this publish changes no substance — a typo, a broken link, formatting. The uploaded `file` may be **JSON or YAML** — the same reader the inline `spec` field and the `sourceUrl` fetch use. It used to be `JSON.parse` alone, answering 400 "convert a YAML spec to JSON first", which is how most people keep a spec. A file that parses but is not an OpenAPI document (no `openapi`/`swagger`, nothing to generate from) is a 422 here too, rather than an empty reference written with a 200.

`mode` is `single | per-operation | per-tag` and `onExisting` is `fail | skip | replace` (default `fail` — this importer writes generated pages in one transaction, so refusing costs nothing and is all-or-nothing). Both used to be cast through unchecked, so a bogus `mode` silently took the single-page branch. `dryRun` and `replaceCollection` take the boolean spellings above; anything else is a 422.

200.description: Import counters. `files` is how many files the request carried — the denominator. `created` (new pages), `replaced` (existing pages rewritten in place), `skipped` (left untouched) and `failed` (could not be turned into a page) are DISJOINT and satisfy `created + replaced + skipped + failed === files`. `imported` is NOT "files processed": it is a convenience total meaning `created + replaced` — the pages this run actually wrote — so it EXCLUDES skipped and failed, and it OVERLAPS `replaced`. That overlap is why three files all rewritten answer `files: 3, created: 0, replaced: 3, imported: 3`: three pages, not six. Sum the disjoint four; never add `imported` to `replaced`. (An earlier version of this page documented `imported + replaced + skipped + failed === files.length`; that invariant is withdrawn — it stopped being true once a replace began counting as an import.) `collisions`/`prunedSlugs`/`plan`/`dryRun` appear when the request asks for them. `redirects` and `retired` appear when a file DECLARED an address change: see the request body for `slug:` and `redirect_from:`. `redirects` lists the rules the run wrote into the space's redirect table; `retired` lists the slugs it moved to the trash because a rule took over their address (reversible with `POST …/{pageId}/restore`). On a dry run both say what WOULD happen and nothing is written.

content.description: Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

replaceCollection.description: Empty the target collection BEFORE importing (hard reset). Prefer `prune` for sync.

onExisting.description: What to do about a slug the SPACE already has (resolved space-wide, never per-collection): `replace` (the default) updates the existing page in place; `fail` writes nothing over it and lists its slug under `refused` (the default of `POST …/openapi/import`, offered here so one explicit value makes both importers behave identically); `skip` leaves it untouched; `rename` is the ONLY value that auto-suffixes to a free slug like `getting-started-2` (opt-in — a page at a URL nobody wrote is the worst docs-as-code outcome); `duplicate` is the legacy spelling of `rename`. An unrecognised value is a 422, never a silent `replace`.

prune.description: Sync mode. After importing, soft-delete (to trash) every live page in this scope the run did not create/replace/skip — so deleting a source file makes its published page disappear. `collection` scopes to the target collection; `space` to the whole space.

dryRun.description: Plan only. Returns what WOULD happen — the same counts (`imported` counts creates AND replaces, so `imported`+`skipped`+`failed` == files.length and `replaced` is a subset of `imported`), a per-file `plan`, cross-collection `collisions`, and the `prunedSlugs` a prune would remove — and writes nothing. `dryRun: true` sets `dryRun` on the response.

schema.description:
**A Markdown file may declare its own address.** Two frontmatter keys are read, and unknown keys are still ignored:

- `slug:` — the address this file lands at, instead of the one its filename spells. Slugified, so `Billing & Plans` and `billing-and-plans` are the same address; a value with nothing a URL can hold in it is refused with the file named, never quietly renamed. Two files declaring one slug is a `422`.
- `redirect_from:` — the addresses this page REPLACES, comma-separated, each rooted and relative to the space's mount (`/old-page`, never `/docs/old-page` — the reader prepends the mount itself). The import writes a redirect rule for each one and moves the page that answered there to the trash, because a rule alone leaves the old page in the sitemap, `llms.txt` and search. Both are reported on the response as `redirects` and `retired`. A self-redirect, a duplicate or a loop is a `422`, exactly as it is on `PUT …/redirects`; an operator's own manual rule for that address is left alone.

post.description:
Writes a batch of pages from Markdown or block JSON in one transaction, creating the collections they need. The door a migration or a git sync drives; it reports what it would do first if you ask for a dry run.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

`onExisting` is `fail | replace | skip | rename | duplicate` and defaults to `replace` (this importer syncs authored files per file, and the first import of a repo routinely lands on the starter page a new space ships with). **An unrecognised value is now a 422** — it used to fall through to `replace`, so a typo chose the destructive option. `fail` refuses to write over an existing page, counts it in `failed`, lists its slug in `refused[]`, and keeps `prune` from deleting it.

On the multipart doors, `dryRun` and the rest are read exactly as strictly as the JSON fields of the same name: `true/false/1/0/yes/no/on/off`, and anything else is a 422. `dryRun=maybe` used to run a REAL import.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

url.description: Where deliveries are POSTed. Must be https outside development, and is called with a signature header your receiver verifies — see the webhooks guide for the scheme.

events.description: The events this endpoint should hear, by name. At least one; `GET /webhooks/events` publishes the whole vocabulary with a sample payload for each.

spaceId.description: Confine the endpoint to one space. Omitted or null means organization-wide, including spaces created after this endpoint.

format.description: The body shape. `json` (the default) sends our own event payload; `slack` and `discord` send a message that platform renders natively, so an incoming-webhook URL from either can be pasted in with nothing in between.

categoryIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload names one of these forum categories. Omitted or null means no filter — the endpoint hears the event wherever it happens.

tagIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload carries one of these tags. Omitted or null means no filter. Tags are matched by name, not by id.

groupIds.description: Narrow group, user and badge events to these groups. Omitted or null means no filter; it has no effect on events that name no group.

bodyEncoding.description: How the delivery body is encoded. `json` (the default) POSTs `application/json`; `form` POSTs `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, for a receiver that cannot parse JSON bodies.

signatureVersion.description: Which signature headers each delivery carries. `v1` is the timestamped scheme alone and is the default for a NEW endpoint; `both` adds the legacy body-only `sha256=`, which is replayable forever and exists only for receivers not yet migrated.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

data.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

minValue.description: Lowest number a voter may pick. With maxValue/step the range must span 2–20 steps.

maxValue.description: Highest number a voter may pick. Must be greater than minValue.

step.description: Spacing between pickable numbers (default 1). Widen it to keep the range inside 20 steps.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Replaced whole on write; unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

minValue.description: Lowest number a voter may pick. With maxValue/step the range must span 2–20 steps.

maxValue.description: Highest number a voter may pick. Must be greater than minValue.

step.description: Spacing between pickable numbers (default 1). Widen it to keep the range inside 20 steps.

closesAt.description: When voting closes. Must be in the future — a past date created an already-closed poll.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Replaced whole on write; unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Replaced whole on write; unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page — the spelling used everywhere else in this API. This endpoint also accepts `pageSize`, which it has always taken; `limit` wins if both are sent. Defaults to 25. 100 is the most it serves — a larger value is capped, not refused, and a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per LANE — not lanes. The lanes are the status columns this board shows, so there is no page two of them; `cursor` goes one page deeper in every lane at once. Defaults to 100. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Defaults to 25. 100 is the most it serves — a larger value is capped, not refused, and a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

200.description: Every published event in this space as a subscribable calendar. Served `inline` so a calendar client can subscribe to the URL, with a one-hour refresh hint. `X-WR-TIMEZONE` appears only when every event agrees on one IANA zone.

text/calendar.example:
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//Forumulate//Events//EN
CALSCALE:GREGORIAN
METHOD:PUBLISH
X-WR-CALNAME:Community Events
REFRESH-INTERVAL;VALUE=DURATION:PT1H
X-PUBLISHED-TTL:PT1H
BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:evt-123@forumulate
DTSTAMP:20260901T000000Z
DTSTART:20260920T130000Z
DTEND:20260920T143000Z
SUMMARY:Launch AMA
DESCRIPTION:Ask the team anything
LOCATION:Online
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR

200.description: A grounded answer, streamed. Frames are NAMED (`token`, `citations`, `done`, `error`), so subscribe per event rather than with `onmessage`. Prose arrives token by token; the `citations` frame carries the anchor-level sources for what was just said; `done` carries the `queryId` to rate the answer with. An error after the first token arrives as an `error` FRAME, not as a status — the status is already committed — and the client falls back to the blocking `docs/ask`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Hits per page. Defaults to 30. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where in the fused list to start. Defaults to 0. 1000 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

200.description:
Success.

This answer carries no `page` object: the unified search: keyword and semantic hits FUSED per request, which is why it publishes `offset` into a ranking rather than a cursor into a collection — the set a token would name is rebuilt for the next query. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Up to 200, or 50 when `include` asks for content — every row then carries a whole piece. Asking for more is capped, not refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `page.next_cursor` of the previous response. Opaque: store it, send it back, never parse it.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only pieces changed after this instant. Pass back the `sync.checkpoint` you stored rather than a clock of your own. An unparseable value is a 422, never a silent full list.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Carry tombstones (`deleted: true`) for pieces removed in the last 30 days, so a removal is discoverable without a full list.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated relations to fold in: `sections` (markdown per named slot) and `body` (the whole piece as markdown). Either one drops the page cap to 50.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated fields to return; everything else is left out. `id` always comes back. Composes with `include`: ask for `include=body&fields=id,contentHash,body` and you get exactly those.

200.description: Two shapes, chosen by the version you state. State `Forumulate-Version` and you get the pieces, the walk (`page`) and the watermark (`sync`). State nothing and you get `{ items }` alone — the legacy shape, served with a `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745: an `@<unix-seconds>` date, not a boolean) and a `Sunset` date, and marked deprecated here so which half is going away is visible on the schema itself.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

post.description:
An `http` check is UP when the request connected AND the response status is below 400 (2xx and 3xx both pass); a `keyword` additionally requires that term in the body, and `certExpiryDays` requires that many days left on the TLS certificate. Set `expectStatus` (100-599) and that EXACT code becomes the only status that counts as up — anything else, 200 included, is down — which is how you watch a dependency whose healthy unauthenticated answer is a 401 or a 405. Null (the default) keeps the under-400 rule. Like `keyword` and `certExpiryDays`, it applies to `http` checks only — a `heartbeat` monitor has no response to inspect and is UP while the job has pinged within `intervalSeconds`.

get.description: `overall` and each component's `status` are the REPORTED state, and three things decide it, in this order: a human's `declaredState` always wins; then the latest check (a failing one is a `major_outage`); then measured history is allowed to degrade a passing check — under 99.5% uptime reads `degraded` and under 97% reads `partial_outage`, so the headline can no longer contradict the percentage printed beside it. History only ever degrades, never improves, and only once `window.sufficient` is true (at least 20 checks spanning at least 6 hours). `window` says what each percentage was actually measured over — `samples`, `daysCovered`, `spanHours` and the first/last check — because `uptime` alone was being printed beside a hardcoded '90 days'. `historyDays` are the day keys the `history` arrays line up with, oldest first. `outages` are the failing runs our own checks recorded, longer than each monitor's `failureThreshold`, whether or not anybody opened an incident for them.

post.summary: Record a heartbeat for a monitor, by POST
post.description: A heartbeat from a scheduled job saying it ran: the signed URL is the whole credential, so a cron line or a CI step can call it with nothing else. Wire it into the job itself — a monitor that has never been pinged reports unknown rather than down.

Records a restart window against the monitor, so the uptime history shows a dip a 60-second poll could never have caught. The token is the same secret as the monitor's heartbeat ping URL. Answers `{ ok: true }` when the window was recorded and `{ ok: false }` for a bad token, an unknown monitor, or a restart folded into one reported seconds earlier.

It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The content tag you believe this resource is at: the `ETag` header where the matching read sets one, otherwise the `contentHash` that read returned. The write is applied only if it still holds, so two editors cannot overwrite each other unnoticed. A list is accepted and any member matching is enough; `*` asserts only that the resource exists. Omit it and the write is unconditional. On every other route a concrete value is a 428 rather than silently ignored.

data.description: The created resource again, under a key that is the same on every create — so a generic client needs one parser rather than one per endpoint. It is the SAME object as the key named after the resource (`page`, `article`, `topic`, …), which remains the canonical name.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

put.description:
Reads one document describing what this organization should have — spaces, their theme, redirects, collections, forum categories, status monitors, and org-level AI knowledge sources — and reports a per-unit DIFF against what is there today. **Nothing is written unless you send `?apply=true`.** Idempotent: applying the same manifest twice does the work once, and the second run answers `unchanged` for every unit. Additive: anything present that the manifest does not declare is reported under `extras` and never deleted. Each block is validated by the schema of the endpoint that owns it, so the manifest accepts exactly what those endpoints accept, and each unit re-checks that endpoint’s own capability — a dry run is refused wherever the apply would be. An apply is NOT one transaction (each subsystem opens its own, which is where tenant isolation lives); it is a sequence of idempotent units that stops at the first failure and names where it stopped, so a partial apply is resumed by fixing the manifest and applying again. The vocabulary for `type`, and which blocks a given type may declare, come from `GET /space-types`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

seed.description: Whether to create the starter structure this kind of space ships with. Left unset it follows who is asking: a console session gets it (an empty space is a worse first screen than an example one), a personal access token does not — an agent creating a space is about to write its own structure, and ours arrives as content it has to find and delete first.

preset.description: One of this space type's named layouts, as published by `GET /space-types`. Unset means the recommended one, resolved at read — so an improvement to the default reaches every space that never chose. An unknown name for the type is a 422 that lists the valid ones.

from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

redirects.description: The whole table, replacing what is stored — except the rules the platform wrote itself when a page or a collection was renamed, which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.
