info.title: Forumulate API
info.description:
The full Forumulate REST API — identity, organizations, spaces, docs authoring, publishing, search, AI, webhooks, and the public reader. Authenticate with a Personal Access Token (Bearer) or the session cookie. Download this spec at `/api/openapi.json` (YAML at `/api/openapi.yaml`) to generate a client SDK (e.g. with openapi-generator).

**Set a non-default `User-Agent` on every request.** The edge WAF challenges requests that carry a default `curl`/library User-Agent (you get a Cloudflare 1010 block, not a JSON error), so a first-time integration silently fails until a custom UA is set — any identifying string (e.g. `my-app-integration/1.0`) passes.

## Conventions

**Organizations take an id or a slug.** `/orgs/{orgId}/…` accepts either the
uuid or the name in `slug`. A name that is not yours is a 404, never a 500.

**Every response is in this document — read the key, never guess it.** Each
operation now publishes its response schema, derived from the handler's own
return type, so the key that holds a list is stated rather than inferred.
Two rules explain the names you will see:

* An ORGANIZATION-level collection is keyed after its path: `/spaces` answers
  `{ spaces }`, `/webhooks` answers `{ webhooks }`, `/orgs` answers
  `{ orgs }` — and `{ organizations }` too, which is what it has always
  answered.
* A SPACE's content is keyed by that space type's own word for a piece, not by
  the path. `GET …/blog` answers `{ articles }`, `…/forum` answers
  `{ topics }`, `…/changelog` answers `{ releases }`, `…/roadmap` answers
  `{ items }`, `…/collections` answers `{ collections }`. The vocabulary is
  published as data at `GET /space-types` (`vocabulary.piece`,
  `vocabulary.container`), so the key for a type you have not integrated yet
  is one request away. Guessing `topics` for a blog has cost one integrator a
  duplicate article; the schema on the operation is the answer.

**State your version and you get the envelope.** Send
`Forumulate-Version: 2026-09-01` and the ENVELOPED collections carry `page`
(`limit`, `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, `total`); walks also carry
`sync.checkpoint`. Send nothing and you get the pre-envelope shape, plus
`Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on THOSE operations saying so. Everywhere
else the header is accepted and changes nothing, and no removal date is sent —
the operations are not deprecated, only the shape they negotiate.

It is universal, and universal is checked rather than claimed: 228 GETs publish a `limit` over rows, and every one
of them but the nine rankings below takes `cursor` and carries `page` for a caller who states a version. That
holds for the 214 whose whole answer IS a collection and for every answer that merely CONTAINS a
collection: a surface's front page (`…/blog`, `…/forum`, `…/roadmap`) pages
the rows it wraps in chrome, and a log that comes with a summary beside it
(`…/api-activity`) pages the log. Three walks over the published document
assert it (`openapi-list-paging.test.ts`): no list without `limit`, no list
without `page`, and nothing that publishes `limit` over rows and then answers
no `page` — so an endpoint added after this sentence is covered by being one.

The nine exceptions are RANKINGS rather than collections — the reputation
leaderboards, every `?q=` search (unified, semantic, per-space), recent
search terms, the search-gap and uncovered-thread reports, and a topic's
related topics — where a score is recomputed per request and so there is no row
a cursor could resume after; they honour `limit` per item, and each one now
carries its own reason on its own answer, in prose and as
`x-forumulate-no-paging`, so you need not come back here to find out why.

`limit` counts the thing you came for. On a GROUPED answer that is not the
groups: the roadmap board's lanes are the status columns it shows, so
`?limit=1` gives you one ITEM in each lane rather than one lane, and a cursor
goes one page deeper in every lane at once.

Every number in this paragraph is counted off the finished document rather than
typed here — a hand tally beside a generated contract drifts by construction,
which is how this page came to claim "9 of 295" while the document said
otherwise.

A route whose two answers really differ answers BOTH shapes and lets you
choose: the pre-envelope body to a caller who states no version, the envelope to
one who does. Every such operation declares the two as an `anyOf` of exactly
two variants — the withdrawn one marked `deprecated` with its removal date,
the other listing `page` as required — and sends `Deprecation`/`Sunset`
only on those. So the set is two lines of the document rather than a list in
this paragraph, which is what it used to be and which was wrong: a shape served
only to unversioned callers used to be published as one object with an optional
`page`, and an optional field cannot be told apart from one that is merely
sometimes absent, nor carry a date. The two are never mixed in one response, so
`page` has exactly one type per answer. Each operation's published response
schema says which it is — that, and not this paragraph, is the thing to code
against.

`page` also carries `has_more` and `next_cursor`, the same two values under
their original spellings. They were the only snake_case keys in an otherwise
camelCase document, which is an inconsistency three integrators reported. They
are deprecated, and deprecated here means dated rather than permanent: state
`2026-11-01` or later and the envelope arrives without them. `2026-09-01` and
the unversioned shape keep them for as long as the policy above says, so there
is nothing to migrate in a hurry — read `hasMore` and `nextCursor`, which are
sent on every version.

A cursor names a row, never an offset, so a walk cannot skip or repeat one when
the set changes under it. Two listings are ranked rather than ordered — the
forum index under `?sort=top` and any listing with `?q=` — and a place in a
ranking is not a place: those answer `nextCursor: null` and continue with
`?page=`.

Four aggregate listings are the stated exception, and the exception is stated
rather than hidden: `/assets`, both member directories and the community tag
feed rank by an aggregate that moves as its window slides, so there is no row a
walk could resume after. Their `nextCursor` is an opaque token carrying the
next PAGE, and it inherits exactly the hazard `?page=` always had there — a
row written mid-walk can shift the set, so one may repeat or be missed at a
page boundary. It is opaque on purpose: when one of them grows an ordering a
cursor can name, it changes underneath you and your code does not.

**A create answers 201, and the envelope is `{ <resource>, data }`.** This is
the one create shape; there is no second one to learn.

    HTTP/1.1 201 Created

    {
      "page": { "id": "…", "title": "…", … },
      "data": { "id": "…", "title": "…", … }
    }

`data` is the KEY TO READ if you are writing one client for many endpoints: it
is on every create that makes a single thing, and it holds the created
resource. The other key — `page`, `article`, `topic`, `pat`,
`webhook`, named after what the collection calls a member — is the canonical
name, is what the operation's schema documents, and is the one to read if you
are integrating one endpoint. They are the SAME object, not a copy: nothing is
renamed, nothing is removed, and a client reading `response.page` is
unaffected. `GET /space-types` publishes the per-type vocabulary if you want
to know a key before you call.

Read `data ?? <the named key>` and you have covered every create, including
the 35 of 156 that answer 201 with no
`data` — because a 201 is not a promise that something addressable was made.
Those are a **result** (an acknowledgement, a computed answer, a tally, a
one-time credential), a
**collection** (the whole list you added to, with no single row to point at) or
a **bare resource** (the resource itself at the top level, with no key beside it
to hang a mirror on). Each one SAYS which it is in its own 201 description, so
you never have to infer it from the shape.

A create may carry more beside those two, and none of it is the resource:
`ok`, `warnings` (a value we accepted and rewrote), `conformance` (a piece
against its shape), `slugChanged` (`{ asked, used }`), and the one-time
secret a credential mint shows you once — `POST /pats` answers
`{ token, pat, data }`, where `token` is the secret and `pat`/`data` are
the row. So: read `data` for the thing that was made, and read the named
siblings for what we did while making it.

**Some creates answer no single resource, on purpose, and have no `data`.**
They are not an oversight, and each one states its own kind on its own 201 — so
the set is read off this document rather than counted here, where a number
would be stale the first time one of them is keyed (two were):

* an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT — `{ ok: true }` from a flag, a subscribe, a consent
  receipt. Nothing was addressed, so there is nothing to return.
* the WHOLE COLLECTION — `POST …/docs/locales` answers every locale, not the
  one you added. `data` meaning "the thing that was made" on
  121 routes and "all of them" on five is
  worse for a generic client than `data` being absent on those
  five.
* a RESULT with no address — an RPC, a search, a quiz attempt, a share-link
  mint (`{ id, token }`), an `archive-to-topic`. There is no row to GET
  back, so there is no resource to mirror.
* TWO resources — `POST …/groups/{groupId}/message` makes a channel and a
  message. Picking one of them to be `data` would be a guess.
* the resource ITSELF, unkeyed — SCIM `POST /scim/v2/Users` and `/Groups`,
  because RFC 7644 defines the response as the resource and a `data` key there
  would make us non-conformant with the spec your IdP implements. These two are
  the only ones left: `POST …/events` and
  `POST …/change-requests/{crId}/comments` were listed here as breaking
  changes waiting for a dated version, and when the callers that reason named
  were checked for, there were none — both answer `{ <resource>, data }` now.

A POST that answers **200** at a collection address is doing something else
again: an upsert (one row per subject, re-sent freely), a toggle, or an RPC.

**`content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES, not a field and a fallback.**
Everything with a body of prose — a forum topic, a blog post, a changelog
release, a roadmap item, and every reply and comment on them — takes it as block
JSON in `content` or as Markdown in `markdown`, converted server-side into
the same blocks. Send ONE. Sending both is a 422 naming `markdown`: nothing
silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise get a
201 and the wrong body. Each of those request bodies is published as a
`oneOf` of the two forms for exactly that reason — it used to be one object
with `content` required and `markdown` optional, which refused a body this
API accepts and permitted one it refuses.

**A named layout is validated against its type's list, which is published.**
`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/preset` takes a `preset` (and sometimes a
`piecePreset`) whose valid values depend on the SPACE's type, so no single
enum on the operation can be right. The list, with a sentence describing each
layout, is at `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` — and the whole vocabulary at
`GET /space-types`. The operation's description enumerates every type's
layouts too, so you can read it without a second request.

**A colour has one spelling per surface, and both are stated.** A THEME token
(`theme.colors.*`) is a six-digit hex with the leading `#` and nothing
else; a bare `0b835b` is a 422 that says so. A COMMUNITY colour — a forum
category, a tag, group flair — is wider, because it ends up in a style
attribute: hex with or without the `#` (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits) or a CSS colour
name, normalised on the way in to the canonical form. `0b835b` is therefore
accepted there and stored as `#0b835b`; it used to be stored exactly as sent,
which is not a colour any browser draws, so the coloured border the guide
promises was simply never there.

**A boolean query parameter is `true`/`false`.** `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`
and `on`/`off` are accepted as well. What is NOT accepted is a value that
looks boolean and is read as something else: `?unhandled=true` once reached a
route that tested for the literal string `1`, so it filtered nothing and
answered 200 with the opposite of what was asked for. Any other value is a 422
naming the parameter.

**`If-Match` is evaluated where it can be, and refused where it cannot.**

Two resources have it, and they have it on EVERY write: a **page** and an
**item**. The tag is the `contentHash` their own reads report, which is also
the `ETag` on the read — one string, from one function, so a tag we just
issued is never refused. Send it as `If-Match` on any write to that resource —
its body, a single slot, its metadata, its slug, its shape, its order, a
publish, an unpublish, a rollback, a schedule, a duplicate, a restore, a
verify, a delete, a purge — and a resource that has moved on answers `412`,
naming both the hash you sent and the one it is at. Re-read and retry.

It took three passes to be able to write that sentence. First only
`PUT …/pages/{pageId}/content` evaluated the header; then the page's own
`PATCH` still answered `428`, so the slug and the metadata — the fields two
people in a console actually race on — had no control at all; then
`PUT …/pages/{pageId}/sections/{key}`, which loads a whole document and swaps
one slot, was still unconditional while its twin on an item was not. A
precondition that holds on some of a resource's doors is one a client cannot
build on, which is why this is now stated as "every write" rather than as a
list of routes.

A write that carries a concrete `If-Match` and CANNOT evaluate it is refused
with `428`; `If-Match: *` passes through, since it only asserts the resource
exists. This is deliberate: the header used to be IGNORED, so a caller who sent
it believed they had optimistic concurrency and lost the write in the exact case
the header exists to catch. What is left on 428 is only what one tag could not
be about — `bulk-delete`, `bulk-move` and `empty-trash`, which address a
selection rather than a resource, and a create, which has no prior state
(`Idempotency-Key` is what makes a create safe to retry). Where another
resource has real concurrency control it is explicit and named — a docs change
request, a theme draft (`theme_draft.stale`, publish with `force`).

**Nothing is dropped in silence.** A field your schema does not recognise is
reported on `X-Unrecognized-Fields` (and refused outright where
`STRICT_BODY_KEYS` is on). The THEME routes
(`PUT|PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/theme` and
`PUT …/reader-themes`) always refuse: a 422 naming the key and its path, e.g.
`chrome.footerColumns.0.title`. A theme key we ignore has no other symptom —
the write answers 200, the read-back echoes what you sent, and only the page
looks wrong — so there is nothing to notice unless we say so. A field we
ACCEPTED but rewrote — a slugified tag,
a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken — is reported on
`X-Field-Warnings` as `field: what we did`, **and in the answer itself as
`warnings[]`**, on every write whose answer is a JSON object. That second
channel is the one that matters to code: the header shipped first and was the
only channel on 77 of the 89 writes that can rewrite something, so a client
that parses JSON — which is all of them — saw a 2xx and nothing else. It is
absent when nothing was rewritten, never `[]`. Both headers are exposed
through CORS. If you get a
2xx and either header is present, the stored value is not the value you sent.

**One code, one status.** The code is the only part of an error to branch on, so
it says what KIND of failure this is — and it appears on exactly one status, so
you never have to read both. `request.malformed` is the 400: the request could
not be understood or was incomplete (a malformed header, an unparseable path
value, a multipart upload with no file part). `validation.failed` is the 422
and nothing else: it was understood and a value is unacceptable. That is the
ordinary one and it carries `details`, keyed by field path. `payload.too_large`
is the 413 (split it), `media.unsupported` the 415 (convert it),
`gone` the 410 (it existed and has been withdrawn — stop asking) and
`precondition.failed` the 412 (re-read and retry); each of those four used to
be `validation.failed` as well, which is how one code came to mean nine
different things. `not_found` is the 404 (a namespaced
`org.not_found`/`space.not_found`/`pat.not_found`/`member.not_found`
only where you must act differently). `conflict` is the 409 over the
resource's STATE — an id taken, a channel closed, a queue item another
moderator claimed. `service_unavailable` is a dependency failing, including a
502/504 from an upstream we called for you: retryable, and it carries
`Retry-After`. `internal` means we have a bug and retrying will not help.
A feature that needs a credential nobody has supplied (`ai.unavailable`,
`atlas.not_configured`) is a **409**, never a 503 — a 503 carries
`Retry-After`, and there is nothing to wait for.

**An error names the field, the allowed values and where to read more.** The
envelope is `{ error: { code, message, details }, requestId }`, where
`details` is keyed by field path. A 422 over a controlled vocabulary lists that
vocabulary in the message (`One of: standard, no-front-door.`) and
`error.docs` links the reference page for the endpoint. `requestId` is the
same value as the `x-request-id` header, repeated in the body because that is
the half of a failure that reaches a bug report — quote it and we can find your
exact request.

**Rate limits are per minute.** Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`,
`RateLimit-Policy` (`600;w=60` — the limit and the window in seconds),
`RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`. A 429 also carries
`Retry-After`.

**A chat/AI connector authenticates as itself.** A connector token
(`Authorization: Bearer fmwc_…`) identifies one connector bound to one
space, so the `/connector/kb/*` endpoints take no `orgId` or `spaceId`
in the path — the token already says which. `GET /connector/kb/manifest`
describes every other endpoint, the capabilities that token actually holds, and
the chunk policy version. This replaces passing a `source` string in a request
body: an author a caller can choose is not an author.

**Removals are discoverable for 30 days.** `include_deleted=true` carries
tombstones, so an incremental sync never has to fall back to a full list to
learn what went away.

**Slots carry roles, and the vocabulary is published.** `GET /roles` returns
the controlled list, each role's canonical reading position and a gloss, plus
what an unroled slot does. It is versioned: a new role is a version bump, not a
silent change to how your articles order themselves.

**Chunks are ours to split.** `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/items/{itemId}/chunks`
returns retrieval-grade chunks with a per-chunk `contentHash`, so you
re-embed what changed rather than everything. The split is a contract once you
store a `chunkId`: `policy.version` changing is a breaking change.

A **chunk's** `contentHash` is a 28-character base36 digest with no prefix —
compare it with the one you stored, and nothing else. It is deliberately not a
cryptographic hash: the splitter runs in the browser too. Everywhere else in
this API — a page, an item — `contentHash` is `sha256:<64 hex>`, which you
may also compare by hand. The two shapes are not comparable with each other,
and neither is comparable across resources: a page hashes its canonicalised
block document, an item the markdown it renders to.

**A webhook signature is a LIST, and you check for membership.**
`X-Forumulate-Signature` carries every signature a delivery has, comma
separated:

    v1,sha256=<hex>, v1,sha256=<hex>, sha256=<hex>, sha256=<hex>

`v1` is HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}` and is the one to
verify — the timestamp is inside the signed base, which is what stops a
captured delivery being replayed. A bare `sha256=` is the legacy body-only
signature; it is replayable by construction and rides along until an endpoint's
`signatureVersion` is set to `v1`. There is one entry per live secret, so a
rotation puts two of each in the header and both verify.

**The body-only `sha256=` entry stops being sent on 2027-10-05.**
It was described as "being retired" with no date, which is not something a
receiver can plan around. After that day a delivery carries `v1` entries
only; `v1` itself does not change, and an endpoint already set to
`signatureVersion: v1` has not been sent a `v0` entry since it was set. If
you check that the header CONTAINS your computed `v1` value, as above, the
date passes without you doing anything.

This paragraph used to describe a single signature, which invited
`header === expected` — and every delivery to an endpoint on the default
`both`, and every delivery during a rotation, then failed to verify. Compute
your `v1` value and check that the header CONTAINS it. There is a tested
implementation in `@forumulate/sdk` — `verifyWebhookSignature`, which
takes the raw body and both headers and returns a boolean:

    const ok = await verifyWebhookSignature({
      secret,
      body: rawBody,   // the RAW bytes. A re-serialised body never verifies.
      signature: headers['x-forumulate-signature'],
      timestamp: headers['x-forumulate-timestamp'],
    });

It checks membership rather than equality, and it rejects a delivery older
than five minutes, which is what the signed timestamp is for.

Also on every delivery: `X-Forumulate-Timestamp`, `X-Forumulate-Event` and
`X-Forumulate-Delivery` (the key to dedupe on — a retry reuses it).
`GET /orgs/{orgId}/webhooks/events` says which event means which change.

pat.description: Atlas API key (`ak_…`, what **Account → Tokens** issues for an Atlas-linked account), Personal Access Token (`cft_…`, the local fallback), OAuth access token (`cfo_…`) or connector token (`fmwc_…`). Opaque strings — there is nothing inside one to parse.

cookie.name: forumulate_session
cookie.description: The browser session cookie, set by signing in and sent automatically by the browser. OpenAPI calls every cookie credential an "apiKey" because that is the only type it has for one — this is NOT an API key: you cannot mint it, copy it into a header, or use it from a server. For that, hold a token (`Authorization: Bearer ak_…` / `cft_…`). Cookie calls are governed by RBAC capabilities rather than by token scopes.

name.description: What this token is for, so a list of them is readable a year later.

scopes.description: `read` to read, `write` to author, `admin` to issue further tokens.

expiresInDays.description: Expire it after this many days. Omit for a token that never expires on its own.

spaceIds.description: The spaces this token may touch. Omit for everywhere its owner can go. A token scoped to one space cannot even list the names of the others — which is what makes it safe to publish.

capabilities.description: Fine-grained capabilities this token may exercise (e.g. `docs.write`), for least privilege. Omit for a token that carries the whole of its owner’s reach. Enforced on top of the scope and the owner’s grants — the token is their intersection.

scopeGrants.description: Named scopes from the published catalog (`GET /pats/scopes`), e.g. `docs:read`, `community:write`, `webhooks:manage`. Each resolves to a bundle of capabilities; the union is stored and enforced exactly like `capabilities`. Omit for a token that carries the whole of its owner’s reach.

constraints.description: Resource-scoped constraints (Discourse ApiKeyScope parity): pin the token to specific space/category/org ids. A request targeting a resource outside the set is denied (403) even when the scope and the owner’s grants would allow it. Omit for an unconstrained token.

lastUsedAt.description: When it was last used to make a request.

spaceIds.description: The spaces it is confined to, when it is.

capabilities.description: The capabilities it is narrowed to, when it is.

scopeGrants.description: The named catalog scopes this token was created with (`docs:read`, …), or null if it named none. Descriptive: `capabilities` above is what is enforced, so re-pointing a scope name at a different bundle can never widen a token that already exists.

applicationName.description: The app holding this key, when it is a device key.

token.description: The token itself. Shown once, on this response, and never again.

limit.description: The limit this page was built with — what was asked for, capped. It is NOT the number of rows returned: a final page under the limit is normal, and `has_more` is the only thing that says whether to keep walking.

hasMore.description: Whether another page follows this one.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to continue. Null on the last page.

has_more.description: The same value as `hasMore`. The only snake_case keys in this API are these two. Sent to callers who state `2026-09-01` or no version at all; ABSENT from `2026-11-01` onwards. Read `hasMore` instead — it is sent on every version.

next_cursor.description: The same value as `nextCursor`. Absent from `2026-11-01` onwards; read `nextCursor`.

total.description: Rows in the whole collection — the size of the set, not of this page, and not of what you have seen so far. ABSENT where the source cannot count the collection: the append-only logs (staff actions, automation runs, connector activity, ingested questions, chat history) grow without bound and are not counted on every page view. Walk on `hasMore`, which is exact on every answer; read `total` only to show a size, and handle its absence.

page.description: Present once a caller states a version.

PatListDto.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

description.description: What granting this scope lets a token do.

applicationName.description: The application/device that will hold this key, e.g. "Forumulate iOS".

scopes.description: `read` to read, `write` to author, `admin` to issue further tokens.

expiresInDays.description: Expire it after this many days.

spaceIds.description: The spaces this key may touch.

capabilities.description: Fine-grained capabilities this key may exercise.

constraints.description: Resource-scoped constraints, as on a PAT.

order.description: Canonical reading position. Lower comes first.

gloss.description: What belongs in a slot of this role, in one line.

version.description: The API version this vocabulary belongs to. A new role is a version bump.

unroledPolicy.description: What to do with a slot carrying no role. `inherit-previous`: it takes the rank of the last roled slot before it, so a verification step stays with the steps it verifies instead of drifting to the end. A slot before the FIRST roled one inherits `summary` (rank 0).

slotKeys.description: A slot KEY is not a role. Roles are this closed, global, six-word vocabulary; keys come from a space’s shape, differ by space type and preset, and an owner may add or omit one. A slot may declare a role and most do not — an unroled slot ranks as `unroledPolicy` says, which means a role filter that ignores the policy silently drops most of a page. The declared key→role mapping for every type and preset is published at `GET /space-types/slots`; one space’s own slots are at `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/shape`.

slug.description: The first segment of every public address this organization owns.

page.description: Present once a caller states a version.

OrgListDto.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

slug.description: The segment this space answers to on a site.

itemCount.description: How many pieces are in it, so a picker can warn before an import.

itemsUpdatedAt.description: When anything in this space last changed, or null for an empty space. `itemCount` says how big a space is; this says whether it is worth walking. Compare it to the value you stored last sync and skip the space entirely when it has not moved.

url.description: Where this space is published — the customer's own domain when they have one, ours otherwise. Null when the space is not public.

data.description: Mirrors `space` — the uniform create envelope.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices about the space just created — e.g. the slug collides with a reserved platform path, so the space is unreachable on our hostname though fine on a custom domain. Absent when there is nothing to warn about.

page.description: Present once a caller states a version.

SpaceListDto.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

tag.description: A meta tag to place on the domain’s home page as proof of ownership.

name.description: The record name to create (the hostname).

value.description: The record value — our edge host (CNAME) or IP (A).

basePath.description: The path this domain publishes under, or '' for the whole hostname.

active.description: True once we ANSWER this address. Separate from `verified`: `POST {domainId}/verify {"activate": false}` proves ownership without switching traffic, so your own application keeps serving the path until `POST {domainId}/activate`.

verificationRecord.description: The TXT record that proves ownership.

verificationFile.description: A file to place on the site as an alternative ownership proof.

dnsTarget.description: The DNS record to create so traffic reaches us (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex); null when the deployment configures no target.

found.description: The A records the hostname currently resolves to.

expected.description: An edge address we accept, when the deployment pins one.

reachesUs.description: True once the hostname resolves to (or CNAMEs to) our edge.

cnameTarget.description: The CNAME target the hostname points at, when it is a CNAME.

path.description: The path prefix to forward to us.

origin.description: The edge origin the proxy must target (origin.forumulate.com), NOT the marketing apex.

mode.description: Which configuration step this domain is on: 'verified' = already reaching our edge (nothing to do); 'dns' = a whole host that must point at us; 'pending' = we are not answering this address yet, either because it is verified but NOT ACTIVATED (your own application still serves it — call `POST {domainId}/activate` when ready) or because it was activated moments ago and routing is still settling; 'path' = an ACTIVATED subfolder that still does not reach us and needs one proxy rule; 'unverified' = a subfolder not verified yet. Only 'path' means "add a proxy rule" — read `message` for which case `pending` is.

served.description: True when traffic already reaches our edge and the domain is serving now.

crawlerBlocked.description: True when a CDN in front of the domain blocks crawler/AI User-Agents, so the (public) docs are invisible to search engines and AI tools until the owner allows bot traffic.

message.description: A one-line, human-readable summary of what to do next (or that nothing is needed).

forward.description: The single reverse-proxy rule to add, when a path-based domain does not yet reach us.

source.description: The integration that reported this standing (e.g. "my-app").

label.description: What this standing is called on the source platform.

value.description: The rank value. Null when the source tracks a tier but no number.

tier.description: A named tier, when the source has one.

profileUrl.description: Link to the member's profile on the source.

iconUrl.description: Icon for the standing, when the source supplies one.

updatedAt.description: When this standing was last pushed.

leaders.description: Members ranked by the source’s value, highest first. The key is `leaders`.

verifiedAt.description: When somebody last said this is still correct. Null means nobody ever has.

ageDays.description: Days since that, or since it last changed when it has never been verified.

stale.description: Whether that exceeds the space's staleness policy.

confidence.description: How much to trust it, 0 to 1. A number rather than a flag because it is meant to be multiplied into your own ranking: recent content should outrank old content without the old disappearing.

kind.description: What backs this piece in storage.

slug.description: The name this piece answers to in an address.

published.description: Whether a reader with no account can see it.

group.description: The collection a page sits in, where the space has more than one.

state.description: An incident's own state, which `published` cannot express.

updatedAt.description: When this piece last changed. What the walk is ordered by, and what `updated_since` compares against.

url.description: Where a reader can see it, or null when the space is not published to an address. Never guess this: a null means "not published", which is a different thing from "we guessed wrong".

contentHash.description: A hash of the content itself, present when `include` was asked for. Diff a whole space from one list request without transferring a body.

deleted.description: Set on a piece that has been removed. See `include_deleted`.

sections.description: Markdown per named slot, when `include=sections` was asked for.

markdown.description: The whole piece as markdown, when `include=body` was asked for.

contentIn.description: WHICH of the two fields above holds this piece's content. Present on every row that carries content. `sections` is populated only for a piece written against a shape; a free-form piece returns `sections: {}`, which a client cannot otherwise tell from a piece that is genuinely empty. Check this rather than assuming: asking for `include=sections` alone on a space of free-form pieces yields nothing and looks like success.

freshness.description: Whether this is still known to be true. Absent on a tombstone and on an incident, which is a record of something that happened and does not go stale.

items.description: The pieces, and nothing else. No cursor, no total, no watermark — this shape cannot express a walk, which is why it is the one being retired.

ItemListLegacyDto.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

checkpoint.description: Store verbatim and send back as `updated_since`. The server defines the watermark so no client has to reason about clock skew.

xp.description: The xp this was derived from (clamped ≥ 0).

currentLevelXp.description: The threshold at which the current level began.

nextLevelXp.description: The next level threshold, or null at the cap.

xpIntoLevel.description: xp accrued since the current level began.

xpForNextLevel.description: xp the current level spans, or null at the cap.

progression.description: Progression per track. Phase 1 has only the shared `default` track.

points.description: The weighted-points total the level is derived from (xp == points).

entitlements.description: Feature/quota gates. Empty in Phase 1 (extension point).

directives.description: Imposed policy (bans, read-only). Empty in Phase 1 (extension point).

xp.description: The new xp total after the fold.

level.description: The level derived from the new xp.

levelChanged.description: True only when this grant moved the user across a threshold.

delta.description: xp actually added (0 on a replay / idempotent no-op).

name.description: Human label, if the grant supplied one.

delta.description: Signed amount actually applied (0 on an idempotent replay).

quantity.description: The quantity held after the fold.

delta.description: Signed quantity actually applied (0 on an idempotent replay).

details.description: Field-level validation problems, keyed by field path (422 only).

docs.description: Where the vocabulary or format this error is about is published — an absolute URL, or an API route such as `GET /space-types/{type}/presets`. Present on errors over a controlled list, so the answer to "what am I allowed to send?" is in the error itself.

slugs.description: The exact slugs that collided, on a slug-conflict 409 — `space.slug_taken`, `page.slug_taken`, `collection.slug_taken`, `site.slug_taken` or `badge.slug_taken`.

requestId.description: The id of this request — the same value as the `x-request-id` and `x-forumulate-request-id` response headers. Quote it in a bug report: it is the only thing that finds your exact request in our logs. It is in the body because that is the part that survives — an SDK that throws the parsed body, a serverless log that keeps the body and drops the headers, a ticket with the JSON pasted in.

BlockNode.description: One node of the document. `type` names the block or inline node — `paragraph`, `heading`, `bulletList`, `codeBlock`, `table`, `hint`, `image`, `text`, … — and `attrs`/`content`/`text`/`marks` depend on it. `GET /docs/block-schema` returns the complete union: every node type, its attributes, which are required, and the values an enumerated attribute accepts. It is public, cacheable, and generated from the same schema this endpoint validates against, so it cannot drift from what a write will accept.

type.description: The node kind, e.g. `paragraph`, `heading`, `codeBlock`, `text`. The full list is at `GET /docs/block-schema`.

attrs.description: Node-specific attributes, e.g. `{ "level": 2 }` for a heading.

text.description: The literal text, for a `text` node.

marks.description: Inline marks (bold, italic, link, …) on a `text` node.

BlockDoc.description: A page as a block document: TipTap/ProseMirror JSON, the canonical content model shared by the editor, the reader and the Markdown converters. Send this as `content` when creating a page or on `PUT /pages/{pageId}/content`. It is the shape `GET /pages/{pageId}/markdown` round-trips from. Author in Markdown instead by sending `body` (whole page) or `sections` (Markdown per named slot) — use exactly ONE of the three.

content.text: Install the SDK, then create your first page.

ConsentPreset.description: The publishable (non-secret) vendor id. Exactly one field is REQUIRED, chosen by `provider`: `cookiemunch`→`cbid`, `cookiebot`→`cbid`, `onetrust`→`dataDomainScript`, `osano`→`customerId`, `termly`→`websiteUuid`. Saving a native provider without its id is a `422 validation.failed` naming the field (e.g. `preset.cbid`). `hosted`/`managed`/`none`/`inherit` take no preset.

cbid.description: CookieMunch site id / Cookiebot domain-group id.

ConsentConfig.description: An org (or, inside a space `override`, a space) consent configuration. Attacker-influenced tenant input, validated hard: no free-text HTML anywhere, and a raw custom loader is accepted only from a host the org has verified.

provider.description: Which CMP renders the banner. `hosted` is our own banner; `managed` provisions a CookieMunch site under our key; `none` is essential-only; `custom` is bring-your-own.

custom.description: For `provider: custom` only. `adapterApi` opens a preference-centre URL (works anywhere); `loader` injects a raw vendor script, allowed ONLY when its host is a verified org domain.

loaderUrl.description: loader: the https loader URL; its host must be a verified org domain.

hosted.description: For `provider: hosted` — structured banner fields (categories, copy, links, theme). Never raw HTML.

webhookSecret.description: Write-only signing secret for this org's inbound consent/DSAR webhook. Set the secret your CMP issued, or POST `consent/webhook-secret` to mint one. Never returned by any GET.

oneOf.description: Inherit the org default.
Override the org default wholesale (same shape as ConsentConfig plus `mode: override`).

SpaceConsentConfig.description: A per-space consent override: inherit the org default, or replace it.

ConsentConfigView.description: Admin view of the stored org config. Secrets never appear — only whether one is set, and whether a signed delivery has been verified.

status.description: Health signal. `active`: a provider is set with every id it needs. `misconfigured`: a provider is set but a required id is missing (a banner will NOT render). `inactive`: `none`/`inherit`/unset.

reason.description: Present when not fully active — why (e.g. `Missing required field preset.cbid …`).

webhookSecretSet.description: Whether an inbound-webhook signing secret exists.

webhookConfigured.description: TRUE once a correctly-signed delivery has been verified — proof the inbound loop works, not merely that a secret exists.

webhookVerifiedAt.description: When the last signed delivery verified.

webhookUrl.description: Where a CMP points its webhook subscription for this org.

ResolvedConsentConfig.description: The non-secret config a reader builds a CMP adapter from — also what `?validate=true` returns without writing.

scriptSources.description: The exact script origins the reader CSP + Trusted Types policy will allow for this provider.

dryRun.description: Present and true on a `?validate=true` response.

ConsentWebhookEvent.description: An inbound consent/DSAR event. Signed with `X-Consent-Signature: sha256=<hex>` (also accepted: `X-CookieMunch-Signature`), an HMAC-SHA256 of the RAW request body keyed with this org's webhook secret; an `X-Consent-Timestamp` may be sent and, if so, `{timestamp}.{body}` is also accepted. Event names: `consent.updated`, `consent.withdrawn`, `dsar.created` (drives the Atlas erase/export bridge), and `consent.test` (the dashboard test event). Verification is timing-safe.

data.description: Event payload; for `dsar.created`: `{ id, type: "deletion"|"access", subjectEmail }`.

PageInfo.description: The paging envelope a collection carries when the caller states `Forumulate-Version`. Each operation’s own response schema says whether it has one: a collection either carries `page`, or answers both this and its pre-envelope shape and picks by the header. No listing pages with keys of its own any more — the allowlists in openapi-collection-shape.test.ts are empty, which is what stops a new one from appearing. Read `hasMore` and `nextCursor`: the snake_case pair beside them is deprecated and is not sent to a caller who states `2026-11-01` or later.

limit.description: The limit this page was built with — what was asked for, capped. NOT the number of rows returned: a final page under the limit is normal, and `hasMore` is the only thing that says whether to keep walking.

hasMore.description: Whether another page follows this one.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to continue. Null on the last page.

has_more.description: The same value as `hasMore`. These two are the only snake_case keys in the API. Sent to callers who state `2026-09-01` or no version at all; ABSENT from `2026-11-01` onwards. Read `hasMore` instead — it is sent on every version.

next_cursor.description: The same value as `nextCursor`. Absent from `2026-11-01` onwards; read `nextCursor`.

total.description: Rows in the whole collection — the size of the set, not of this page, and not of what you have seen so far. ABSENT where the source cannot count the collection: the append-only logs (staff actions, automation runs, connector activity, ingested questions, chat history) grow without bound and are not counted on every page view. Walk on `hasMore`, which is exact on every answer; read `total` only to show a size, and handle its absence.

ForumulateVersion.name: forumulate-version
ForumulateVersion.description:
API version negotiation. **Optional**, and accepted on every operation. Send a dated version like `2026-09-01` to opt into the paginated envelope (`page`, `sync.checkpoint`); omit it and you receive the pre-envelope legacy response shape. Accepted values are dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` form; a malformed value is a 400, an unknown-but-date-shaped value resolves to the shape in effect on that day.

On most operations this header changes nothing — they answer one shape to everybody. The operations that negotiate a shape are the ENVELOPED collections, and those are the ones whose responses carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` when you state no version; each declares all three as response headers, so look there rather than assuming. The pre-envelope shape is deprecated as of `2026-09-01` and is served until **2027-09-01**. After it, a request that states no version receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Nothing else is going away: the paths, the parameters and the error envelope are unaffected, and the operations themselves are not deprecated — only the shape, which is marked `deprecated` on the schema that is being withdrawn.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes this write safe to retry. **Optional** — send any unique string (a UUID is ideal) and the first request runs while its response is remembered under that key for 24 hours; an identical retry replays that same status and body instead of acting twice, so a timeout or a 5xx from the edge can be retried without creating a second row. A retry sent while the first request is still in flight is refused with `409`. The key is scoped to the method and path, so the same key on a different endpoint is a different request. Error responses of 5xx are never cached — those retries re-run. A key is bound to the BODY it was first used with: reusing it with a different body is a `409 idempotency.key_reused`, not a replay, because replaying would tell you a write landed that never ran. Generate one key per request, never per process or per session.
